document.title: Temperature and nitrogen regulation of Escherichia coli growth

research_question.question: How do nitrogen availability and temperature regulate the specific growth rate of Escherichia coli in continuous culture?
research_question.scope: Continuous and batch cultures of Escherichia coli K-12 across three temperatures and a range of ammonium concentrations.

evidence.quote: We investigated how nitrogen availability and temperature regulate the specific growth rate of *Escherichia coli* in continuous culture.

study_profile.organism_or_system: Escherichia coli K-12 in minimal medium
study_profile.study_design: Batch and chemostat experiments with three independent biological replicates per condition
study_profile.sample_scale: Three temperatures and ammonium concentrations from 0.1 to 10 mM
study_profile.time_scale: Exponential growth and continuous-culture steady state

variables.definition: Temperature at which the culture was maintained.
variables.relationship: Hypothesized to increase the maximum specific growth rate.

evidence.quote: *Escherichia coli* K-12 was grown in minimal medium. Ammonium chloride was the sole nitrogen source. The dilution rate was set to 0.2 per hour in chemostat cultures. Temperature was controlled at 25, 30, or 37 degrees Celsius.

variables.notes: Treated as an experimental factor in this extraction.

variables.definition: Availability of nitrogen to the culture, operationalized through ammonium concentration and limitation state.
variables.value_or_range: Limited versus replete; ammonium 0.1 to 10 mM
variables.relationship: Regulates the specific growth rate and the half-saturation constant.

evidence.quote: We investigated how nitrogen availability and temperature regulate the specific growth rate of *Escherichia coli* in continuous culture.
We hypothesized that the maximum specific growth rate increases with temperature and that the half-saturation constant for nitrogen decreases under nitrogen limitation.

variables.notes: The paper combines a continuous concentration range with a limitation/replete classification.

variables.definition: Natural logarithm of optical density change per unit time.
variables.value_or_range: Not reported as a full range
variables.relationship: mu = d(ln OD600)/dt; modeled as a function of N_avail and T.

evidence.quote: Optical density at 600 nm was converted to cell dry weight using a calibration curve. The specific growth rate was calculated as the natural logarithm of optical density change per unit time.

variables.notes: The symbol mu follows the Monod convention used in the source.

variables.definition: Upper limit of the specific growth rate in the Monod model.
variables.relationship: mu = mu_max S / (K_s + S); hypothesized to increase with T.

evidence.quote: At 30 degrees Celsius, the maximum specific growth rate was 0.61 per hour and the half-saturation constant for ammonium was 0.42 mM.

variables.definition: Substrate concentration at which the specific growth rate is half of the maximum specific growth rate.
variables.relationship: mu = mu_max S / (K_s + S); decreased under nitrogen limitation.

evidence.quote: At 30 degrees Celsius, the maximum specific growth rate was 0.61 per hour and the half-saturation constant for ammonium was 0.42 mM.
